query: How can we reduce declined travel expenses?

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: A scoping/filter flag identifying travel-related records; already implied by the query's focus on travel expenses. Not an intervenable treatment nor a confounder.

per_column.name: expense_category
per_column.rationale: Categorical classification of expense type, implied by the query. It is a descriptive attribute, not a settable lever affecting decline status.

per_column.name: entry_origin
per_column.rationale: How an expense enters the system (manual procurement vs automated system vs travel claim) is a configurable process choice an actor could change to affect decline rates; intervenable.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: Whether a source id is attached is a data-completeness property that could plausibly be enforced/set as a policy, potentially affecting acceptance; a weak but settable lever.

per_column.name: ci_specificity
per_column.rationale: How specifically the configuration item is described is a settable data-quality lever (require specific model vs placeholder) that could influence decline; intervenable.

per_column.name: processing_lag_category
per_column.rationale: Processing speed is an operational lever an actor could change; it can plausibly affect decline status. Intervenable, though it risks being a mediator/collider depending on timing.

per_column.name: expense_action_type
per_column.rationale: Descriptive classification of the action; largely an intrinsic attribute of the expense rather than a settable lever.

per_column.name: submitting_department
per_column.rationale: Department drives both submission practices (treatment) and decline outcomes; a common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: asset_brand
per_column.rationale: Brand of hardware asset is largely irrelevant to travel expense declines and not a settable travel lever; not a confounder for the travel outcome.

judge.rationale: The set includes at least one genuinely intervenable lever (entry_origin, has_source_id, ci_specificity, processing_lag), satisfying claim (a) weakly. However, most columns are scoping flags or descriptive attributes rather than levers, and several are more relevant to hardware/asset records than to travel expenses. Claim (b) is barely met: only submitting_department functions as an unnamed common cause of both a submission-process lever and decline outcome. There is no adjustment for co-determinants like expense amount magnitude, policy compliance, approver, or claimant experience that would confound the treatment-outcome relationship. The confounding structure is thin, so the what-if identification is weak.
